payload.rewritten_goal:
You are coordinating a team of healthcare agents for a prenatal prescription consultation for Soraya Bhatt. Reference entity IDs: case id, client id, request id. The encounter includes a provided first-trimester urgent-care note evidence summary, a photo of an over-the-counter cold/flu combination box, and an outside ultrasound report image provided by the patient MANDATORY steps: 1. review the current pregnancy history, medication timeline, and social context for while reconciling the provided medication packaging and urgent-care note; 2. obtain the authorized lab panel and focused exam findings relevant to dehydration, infection severity, and pregnancy-safe prescribing; 3. obtain an obstetric-focused specialty interpretation on whether the requested medication plan is safe in early pregnancy and what alternatives are preferred; 4. record the working prescription-safety assessment and reasoning; 5. issue the triage recommendation and prepare a patient-facing summary with the safest medication plan and follow-up guidance.

Relevant document evidence summaries are inlined below:
- HC 041 urgent care first trimester note: Urgent-care encounter note documenting current pregnancy status, symptoms, prior instructions, and a proposed medication plan that must be reconciled. Extracted content: Hc-041 Urgent Care First Trimester Note Urgent-care encounter note documenting current pregnancy status, symptoms, prior instructions, and a proposed medication plan that must be reconciled. Details Case ID HC-041 appears on the note header. Client ID PT-HC-041 appears on the note header for Soraya Bhatt. Request ID RXR-59288 is referenced as the medication review follow-up request. The note states the patient is in the first trimester with positive home pregnancy test and known intrauterine pregnancy under outside OB follow-up. The HPI documents 3 days of cough, nasal congestion, sore throat, subjective fever, and reduced oral intake with nausea. The note documents concern for dehydration due to poor intake and lightheadedness. The assessment lists presumed viral upper respiratory infection and advises avoidance of NSAIDs in pregnancy. The plan recommends an over-the-counter cold/flu combination product from the provided box photo, creating a medication-safety reconciliation need. The note also mentions acetaminophen as a fever/pain option and encourages hydration. The medication list in the note includes prenatal vitamin and pyridoxine/doxylamine use for nausea earlier in pregnancy. The social context documents that the patient works in a daycare with multiple sick contacts at home/work. The note includes a disclaimer that pregnancy-safe medication selection should be confirmed with obstetric care. Additional Information a realistic 2-page outpatient urgent-care document clinical note Use a standard medical note layout with header, patient identifiers, HPI, ROS, meds, assessment, and plan these exact identifiers in the header: Case ID HC-041, Client ID PT-HC-041, Request ID RXR-59288, patient name Soraya Bhatt social history noting daycare employment and sick contacts
